newsitem.title: MEXICO: Zedillo says won't relax pace in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Zedillo says won't relax pace in Mexico.

text.p: The Mexican economy is showing encouraging signs of recovery, but the government is not about to relax its pace, President Ernesto Zedillo said on Tuesday.
"The indicators are certainly encouraging, but they are by no means enough. By no means will they make us relax our pace," Zedillo said at a ceremony in honour of ISSSTE social security workers
"Today, the recovery is spreading to all productive sectors in the economy. Production has stopped falling and is beginning to grow once more," he added.
Mexico suffered a sudden and unexpected devaluation of the peso in December 1994, days after Zedillo took office. That triggered the worst recession the Mexican economy had seen in six decades.
"Today, employment is developing favorably," Zedillo said, referring to open unemployment of 5.3 percent for August, compared to a year-ago level of 7.6 percent.
The government has to persevere in its economic program until the recovery is consolidated and economic growth considerably outstripped population growth, Zedillo said.
"We must persevere in strengthening domestic savings so as to depend less on foreign capital, so as to definitely avoid the recurrence of economic crises," Zedillo said.
Some economists feel that the December 1994 peso crisis was preceded by investors withdrawing their money from Mexico and leaving the country's foreign currency reserves very low.
Although Zedillo has recently trumpeted Mexico's economic recovery by citing macroeconomic figures, many analysts point out that the slide in most Mexicans' purchasing power has not recovered much.
